---
title: "Day 4: Metagenomics"
author: "Minh-Quan Ton-Ngoc, Hao Chung The"
date: "2026-05-15"
---

Day 4 introduces metagenomic sequencing as a practical tool for diagnosis and clinical decision-making. The lessons use compact teaching re-analyses so that you can focus on the workflow, interpretation, and limitations without needing to reproduce full published studies during the workshop.

In [Clinical Foundations & AMR Surveillance](vietnamese-healthy-gut-microbiome.qmd), you will analyse 6 stool microbiome samples adapted from Pereira-Dias et al. (Journal of Infectious Disease, 2021). The exercise uses a subset of a Vietnamese healthy gut microbiome and antimicrobial resistance surveillance dataset to show how shotgun metagenomic reads can be processed into taxonomic and AMR summaries.

In [Actionable Diagnostics & Clinical Reasoning](clinical-reasoning.qmd), you will move to a clinical metagenomics case. This focuses on analysis and interpretation of unbiased sequencing, and how metagenomic evidence supports clinical reasoning rather than replacing it.

::: {.callout-note}
## Technical note

The Day 4 practical exercises use R 4.5.0 and Python 3.13. The Python examples also require `numpy` and `pandas`.
:::
